lake_mead_TEMP.band_meaning: Shaded band: the 95% range of the straight-line trend, i.e. where the true trend line most likely lies. It is not the range of the monthly values.
lake_mead_TEMP.method: Seasons removed (each month minus its calendar-month average), then a straight-line trend; the 95% interval and t-test p-value are corrected for month-to-month correlation. Checked with a seasonal Mann-Kendall test and seasonal Sen's slope. 'Years until significant' is a planning estimate that assumes the trend and the noise stay the same; it is not a forecast.

explain.headline: Air temperature in Lake Mead (USA) · Significant increase (+0.376 °C per decade)
explain.details: After removing seasonal swings, the straight line estimates +0.376 °C per decade over 2001–2024. The line's estimated change from start to finish is +0.9 °C. The shaded 95% band shows uncertainty around the line. The 95% range for its rate is +0.0771 to +0.675 °C per decade. The p-value is 0.014. If the underlying rate were zero, the p-value tells us how often the test would see evidence at least this strong just by chance.
explain.caveat: A straight line simplifies a record that can rise and fall over time. Identifying the cause requires a separate investigation.
